title: Scheme ampleness characterized by the canonical section-algebra Proj map
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Say $L$ is $f$-ample if, for every affine open $V\subseteq T$, $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; quasi-compactness of $f$ is part of this notion. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $L$ is $f$-ample; (2) $f$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and, for the canonical graded algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes n}$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], the relative Proj $P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj], and the evaluation map $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n}$, one has $U(\psi)=X$ and $r_{L,\psi}:X\to P$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Here $f^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], $f_*N(V)=N(f^{-1}(V))$, and $U(\psi),r_{L,\psi}$ are the generation locus and canonical map of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] on schemes. The algebra and map in (2) are formed only after its quasi-separatedness condition is imposed; the algebra is then quasi-coherent. Equivalently, this algebra is $f_*(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n})$ with the grading by tensor degree. Moreover, either condition implies that $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: Assume (1). For each affine open $V\subseteq T$ put $W=f^{-1}(V)$. The sheaf $L|_W$ is ample by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated] says $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. Apply the cancellation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] to $W\to V\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: the morphism $W\to V$ is separated. No quasi-separatedness of $f$ was assumed.

These affine restrictions imply that $f$ is separated: the opens $W\times_VW$ cover $X\times_TX$, and on each of them the diagonal of $f$ is the closed-immersion diagonal of $W\to V$. Closedness of its image, the identification with that image, and surjectivity of the structure-sheaf map glue on this open cover, exactly the closed-immersion definition [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus its diagonal is a closed immersion, the definition of separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its inverse image of any affine open is affine, by the affine-quotient clause of [def-weil-closed-immersion], and is therefore quasi-compact. The diagonal is consequently quasi-compact, which is precisely quasi-separatedness [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01VI, locality of separatedness; Tag 01VJ, separation before pushforward

proof.text: Construct the algebra whenever $f$ is quasi-separated, either as just proved under (1), or as explicitly required under (2). Each $L^{\otimes n}$ is locally free of rank one by a trivialization of $L$ and hence quasi-coherent [def-sc-invertible-module]. The qcqs pushforward theorem [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] applies: quasi-compactness is the standing hypothesis and quasi-separatedness has now been supplied. Thus every $f_*L^{\otimes n}$ is quasi-coherent, and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure] makes their sum quasi-coherent. Tensor multiplication and the unit define its graded algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. For the alternate expression $f_*(\bigoplus_nL^{\otimes n})$, the same coproduct-closure node makes the sum upstairs quasi-coherent, so qcqs pushforward makes its image quasi-coherent. For affine $V\subseteq T$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) gives qcqs for the base change $W=f^{-1}(V)\to V$, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] gives qcqs for the scheme $W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum] with $p=0$ on $W$. The resulting equality of affine sections identifies these two algebras, with the same products. This justifies the exact canonical algebra used in the source.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, construction of the graded canonical algebra; Schemes Tag 01LC

proof.text: The relative Proj exists and restricts over every affine $V\subseteq T$ to $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A(V))$, by [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. Evaluation sends a local section of $f_*L^{\otimes n}$ to that same section of $L^{\otimes n}$, and commutes with tensor products and the unit. Apply [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] to obtain $U(\psi)$ and its canonical $T$-morphism $r$. Its restriction to each affine base open is the usual scheme canonical morphism for the graded map into the section ring; here that map is the identity $\mathcal A(V)=\Gamma_*(f^{-1}(V),L|_{f^{-1}(V)})$. The affine restriction and compatibility clauses are used, not an unsupported flat base-change assertion for a non-qcqs morphism.

Continue under (1). On $W=f^{-1}(V)$ every point has a nonvanishing homogeneous section of $L|_W$ by the ample-sheaf definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Such a section generates its rank-one stalk, so this point is in the generation locus of evaluation. The restriction compatibility in [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] therefore gives $U(\psi)\cap W=W$ for all affine $V$, and hence $U(\psi)=X$.

For each affine $V$, apply [lem-sc-ample-proj-local-chart] to $W=f^{-1}(V)$ and $L|_W$. Its hypotheses hold by (1), and it says the canonical map has preimage $W_s$ of $D_+(s)$ and is an isomorphism $W_s\to D_+(s)$ whenever $W_s$ is affine. The ample-sheaf definition supplies such affine $W_s$ covering $W$. Thus the canonical map identifies $W$ with the union of these basic opens: the local inverses agree on overlaps because their composites with the same map are identities and these are its full basic-open preimages. By the scheme interpretation and affine restriction in [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map], this is exactly $r|_W$. These image opens, as $V$ varies, form an open subset of $P$, and the local inverses glue there. Hence $r:X\to P$ is an open immersion. This proves (2), including its quasi-separatedness clause from step 2.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, (3) implies (5), using Properties Tags 01PZ and 01Q1

proof.text: Conversely assume (2), and fix an affine open $V\subseteq T$. Put $W=f^{-1}(V)$, $M=L|_W$, and $A=\mathcal A(V)$. The restriction of $r$ identifies $W$ with an open subscheme $O\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(A)$, by [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] and the affine scheme compatibility of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map]. This open is quasi-compact because $f$ is quasi-compact. The restricted map is the canonical map for $A\to\Gamma_*(W,M)$, and its positive-degree sections generate everywhere because $U(\psi)=X$. Apply [lem-trf-proj-canonical-map-twist-comparison] to get $d>0$ and $r_V^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Proj}(A)}(dk)\simeq M^{\otimes dk}$ for every $k>0$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, (4) implies (1), affine restriction and twist comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] to the quasi-compact open $O$: choose $e>0$ so that $\mathcal O_O(ek)$ is invertible ample for every $k>0$. Use $k=d$ here and $k=e$ in step 7. Then $M^{\otimes de}$ identifies with the ample sheaf $\mathcal O_O(de)$ under the isomorphism $W\simeq O$. The isomorphism transports its sections, nonvanishing opens, and their affineness, so the ample-sheaf definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] gives ampleness of $M^{\otimes de}$ on $W$. Any section of $(M^{\otimes de})^{\otimes n}$ is a section of $M^{\otimes den}$ with the same nonvanishing open. Since $de>0$, the same affine section cover therefore proves that $M$ is ample. This uses the easy positive-power-to-original direction directly and never assumes $\mathcal O(1)$ invertible.

The preceding argument proves $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ ample for every affine open $V\subseteq T$. Along with the standing quasi-compactness of $f$, this is (1). Applying steps 1 and 2 again gives the additional separatedness conclusion under (2) as well.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01VH, 01VI, 01VJ, equivalence (1) and (5); forward: derive separation, then qcqs pushforward and affine canonical charts; reverse: (4) implies (1).
